name: Crown
overview: The Bible presents crowns as significant symbols of authority, holiness, and honor, often associated with priests, kings, and queens. For instance, the priests wore a holy crown made of pure gold set upon a mitre as commanded by God (Exodus 29:6; Exodus 39:30; Leviticus 8:9), signifying their consecration and dedication. Kings and queens similarly wore crowns as marks of royal dignity and favor, as seen when Queen Vashti and Esther were adorned with royal crowns to display beauty and honor before the people (Esther 1:11; Esther 2:17; Esther 6:8). These crowns, sometimes described as ornaments set with gems or made of gold, carry both literal and symbolic meanings, representing victory, authority, and divine approval.
